This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user is building multi-dimensional componentisation into a conversation context viewer app. This session focused on:
   - Fixing the waffle chart to show a single blended chart with tuple-based legends (pairs/triads) instead of separate per-dimension charts
   - Fixing the "default" dimension disappearing when adding a new dimension
   - Making component filters work across all dimensions with AND logic
   - Showing multi-dimension component badges in conversation view
   - Grouping filter checkboxes by dimension
   - Fixing "Generate analysis" to auto-generate summary first when missing
   - Adding multi-dimension support to import/export
   - Fixing stale waffle chart when new dimension completes processing
   - Making workflow section show tuple legends
   - Writing regression tests for export/import

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - `DimensionData` interface: `{ name, prompt, components, componentMapping, componentTimeline, componentColors, customComponents?, customColoringPrompt? }`
   - Tuple-based component keys: e.g. `"workflow:project_context|error_types:ruff_check"` for multi-dimension waffle chart
   - AND filtering logic: a part is hidden if ANY of its components (across all dimensions) is unchecked
   - Color blending via `blendColors()` for multi-dimension waffle squares
   - `activeDimensionsKey` (serialized string) instead of Set reference for useMemo deps
   - Backward-compatible export format: `dimensions` field is optional on both parts and FileExport
   - Legacy field sync: `syncLegacyFieldsFromDimensions` falls back to first dimension if "default" renamed
   - `ensureDimensions` only migrates legacy fields when dimensions dict is completely empty

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **`src/components/ComponentsView.tsx`** — Central component for waffle chart and workflow visualization
     - Replaced per-dimension waffle charts with single blended chart using tuple keys
     - Added `activeDimensionsKey` for stable useMemo deps
     - `tupleData` useMemo computes `Record<string, number>` where keys are `"dim1:comp1|dim2:comp2"`
     - `getTupleColorStyles` returns blended colors per tuple
     - `messageComponents` now produces tuple keys when multi-dim active
     - Added `WorkflowTupleLegend` component for tuple-based workflow legend
     - Removed `MultiDimensionLegend` component (replaced by tuple approach)
     ```typescript
     const activeDimensionsKey = [...activeDimensions].sort().join(",");
     
     const tupleData = useMemo(() => {
       if (!dimensions || activeDimensions.size <= 1) return null;
       const activeDimNames = [...activeDimensions].sort();
       const tupleTokens: Record<string, number> = {};
       // ... builds tuple keys from all active dimensions per part
       return { tupleTokens, total };
     }, [dimensions, activeDimensionsKey, conversation.messages, currentMessageIndex, filteredPartIds, messageTypeFilters]);
     ```

   - **`src/components/WaffleChart.tsx`** — Added `hideLegend?: boolean` prop (currently unused but available)

   - **`src/components/ConversationView.tsx`** — Conversation view with filters
     - Component filter dropdown groups checkboxes by dimension when `dimensions && Object.keys(dimensions).length > 1`
     - All 4 filter locations use AND logic: collect all components across all dimensions for a part, hide if any is unchecked
     - Added `dimensions` to `SourceWorkflowState` interface
     - Added `effectiveAutoComponentMapping` and `selectedAutoComponentMatchesPart` (user's manual edits for tuple selection support)
     ```typescript
     // AND logic: hide part if ANY component is unselected
     const partComponents: string[] = [];
     const legacyComp = componentMapping[part.id];
     if (legacyComp) partComponents.push(legacyComp);
     if (dimensions) {
       for (const dim of Object.values(dimensions)) {
         const dc = dim.componentMapping[part.id];
         if (dc && !partComponents.includes(dc)) partComponents.push(dc);
       }
     }
     if (partComponents.length === 0 || partComponents.some(c => !selectedComponents.has(c))) {
       return false;
     }
     ```

   - **`src/components/MessagePartView.tsx`** — Shows badges from ALL dimensions (not just active)
     - Changed condition from `activeDimensions.size > 1` to `dimNames.length > 1`
     ```typescript
     const dimNames = dimensions ? Object.keys(dimensions) : [];
     const dimensionBadges = dimensions && dimNames.length > 1
       ? dimNames.map((dimName) => { ... })
       : null;
     ```

   - **`src/App.tsx`** — Central state management (3100+ lines)
     - `syncLegacyFieldsFromDimensions`: Falls back to first dimension if "default" doesn't exist
     - `ensureDimensions`: Only migrates when `Object.keys(ctx.dimensions).length === 0`
     - `handleAddDimension`: Migrates legacy fields to "default" dimension before adding new one
     - `createAnalysisActivity`: Collects components from ALL dimensions, relaxed guard (no `componentTimeline` requirement), added diagnostic logging
     - Auto-generates summary before analysis when `aiSummary` is missing
     - `handleGenerateAnalysis` passes `onSummaryChunk` callback
     - `components` prop to ConversationView merges from all dimensions
     - `sourceWorkflowStates` includes `dimensions`
     - Preset export includes per-dimension prompts
     - Import restore rebuilds `DimensionData` from imported dimensions
     ```typescript
     // handleAddDimension fix
     let dims = { ...(conv.dimensions || {}) };
     if (Object.keys(dims).length === 0 && conv.components) {
       dims["default"] = {
         name: "default", prompt: conv.customPrompt,
         components: conv.components || [], componentMapping: conv.componentMapping || {},
         componentTimeline: conv.componentTimeline || [], componentColors: conv.componentColors || {},
       };
     }
     ```

   - **`src/lib/export-schema.ts`** — Zod schemas for export format
     - Added `dimensions` to `ExportPartSchema`: `z.record(z.string(), z.string()).optional()`
     - Added `ExportDimensionSchema`: `{ components, colors, prompt?, coloringPrompt? }`
     - Added `dimensions` to `FileExportSchema`: `z.record(z.string(), ExportDimensionSchema).optional()`

   - **`src/lib/export-builder.ts`** — Export building functions
     - `buildConversationWithComponents` embeds per-dimension component mappings on each part
     - `buildFileExport` includes per-dimension colors/prompt/components when multiple dimensions exist
     - Added `DimensionData` to WorkflowState interface

   - **`src/parsers/context-viewer-parser.ts`** — Import parser
     - `extractMetadata` now returns `dimensions` field from file export

   - **`src/parser.ts`** — Parser types
     - Added `dimensions` to `ConversationMetadata` interface

   - **`src/ai-summary.ts`** — Analysis generation
     - `generateContextAnalysis` accepts optional `dimensions` parameter
     - Generates per-dimension CSV data when multiple dimensions exist

   - **`vitest.config.ts`** — New file, vitest configuration with `@` path alias

   - **`src/lib/__tests__/export-import.test.ts`** — New test file (just written, not yet run)
     - Schema validation tests against real exports from `../long-prompts-analysis/context-viewer-exports/`
     - ContextViewerParser tests (canParse, parse, extractMetadata)
     - Single-dimension round-trip test
     - Multi-dimension round-trip test
     - Backward compatibility test (old export without dimensions)
     - Session export test

4. Errors and Fixes:
   - **`filteredPartIds` used before declaration**: Moved `perDimensionTokens` useMemo after `filteredPartIds` declaration
   - **TS2322 in export-builder.ts**: `Record<string, unknown>` didn't match ExportPart type. Fixed by using `ExportPart` type explicitly
   - **TS2339 `dimensions` not on SourceWorkflowState**: Added `dimensions?: Record<string, DimensionData>` to the interface
   - **Generate analysis silently failing**: Guard required `componentTimeline?.length` which was empty. Relaxed guard, but real issue was missing `aiSummary`. Added auto-generate summary before analysis
   - **Default dimension disappearing**: `handleAddDimension` used `{ ...(conv.dimensions || {}) }` which created empty dict when dimensions hadn't been explicitly created yet. Fixed by migrating legacy fields to "default" first
   - **Component filter only worked for default dimension**: Changed all 4 filter locations to check all dimensions' componentMapping
   - **Waffle chart not updating when new dimension completes**: `useMemo` deps included Set reference which isn't reliably compared by React. Added `activeDimensionsKey` string serialization
   - **User feedback on filter logic**: User explicitly asked for AND logic — "if one component is unselected, it should not appear, even if the segment has other components which are not filtered"

5. Problem Solving:
   - Solved single blended waffle chart with tuple-based approach
   - Solved dimension rename bug by making legacy sync use first dimension as fallback
   - Solved analysis generation by auto-generating summary first
   - Solved stale waffle with string-serialized Set for memoization
   - Export/import backward compatibility via optional `dimensions` field

   - "Can you test it by running an export and then importing it? this directory has some exports from the past... structure these as a test so we can re-run them for regression etc. I can also give you a multi dimension export in a bit."

The project uses the [Vercel AI SDK](https://sdk.vercel.ai/) (`generateText` and `streamText` from `"ai"`). The `result` object from both functions includes a `usage` property with `promptTokens`, `completionTokens`, and `totalTokens` — but **not cost in dollars**. The AI SDK doesn't return monetary cost directly since pricing varies by provider/model.

However, you have the token counts available on every result:
- `result.usage.promptTokens`
- `result.usage.completionTokens`
- `result.usage.totalTokens`

You could compute cost from these if you know the per-token pricing for the model being used. The OpenAI provider also passes through any provider-specific metadata, but OpenAI's API itself doesn't return cost data either — just token counts.

content.thinking:
The user is asking a great architectural question. Let me think about this.

The core issue is that `markComplete` and `updateState` in `WorkflowRunner` write ALL fields from `ctx` back to the conversation state, even fields that the current workflow event didn't touch. So when you run "Generate Analysis" (which only needs to update `analysis`), it also overwrites `dimensions`, `components`, `componentColors`, etc. with whatever was on `ctx` — and if `ctx` was constructed without `dimensions`, it gets set to `undefined`.

This is a "write-everything-back" pattern where every workflow completion overwrites the entire conversation state, rather than only writing back the fields that were actually modified.


The fix is to track which fields each workflow event actually modifies, then only write those fields back to the conversation state instead of blindly overwriting everything.

I have enough information. Here is the implementation plan.

---

## Implementation Plan: `src/aggregation.ts`

### Overview

Create a single module that consolidates all pure token-counting, percentage, timeline-building, and CSV-generation logic. The module has no React imports and no AI/API calls. Every function is a pure transformation of `Conversation` + mapping data into numeric aggregates.

### Proposed API

The module exports these functions and re-exports the types/constants it absorbs:

#### Types (defined here, re-exported from componentisation.ts for backward compat)

```ts
// Already exists in componentisation.ts, move here:
export interface ComponentTimelineSnapshot {
  messageIndex: number;
  componentTokens: Record<string, number>;
  totalTokens: number;
}

// New shared type for the common aggregation result
export interface ComponentAggregation {
  componentTokens: Record<string, number>;
  totalTokens: number;
}

// New type for percentage-decorated component data
export interface ComponentPercentage {
  component: string;
  tokens: number;
  percentage: number;  // 0-100
}
```

#### Constants (moved from componentisation.ts)

```ts
export const TUPLE_SEPARATOR = " · ";
```

#### Function 1: `getPartTokenCount`
Replaces the duplicated `("token_count" in part && part.token_count) || 0` pattern (appears in 8+ files).

```ts
export function getPartTokenCount(part: { token_count?: number }): number
```

#### Function 2: `getMessageTokenCount`
Replaces `getTotalTokens()` in MessageView.tsx and `getMessageTokens()` in ConversationView.tsx.

```ts
export function getMessageTokenCount(message: Message): number
```

Implementation: `message.parts.reduce((sum, part) => sum + getPartTokenCount(part), 0)`

#### Function 3: `aggregateComponentTokens`
The core building block. Replaces the duplicated loop pattern in export-builder.ts (lines 141-151), App.tsx (lines 1388-1433), ComponentsView.tsx (lines 197-222), StaticComponentsView.tsx (lines 56-74), and ConversationView.tsx (lines 482-552).

```ts
export function aggregateComponentTokens(
  conversation: Conversation,
  componentMapping: Record<string, string>,
  options?: {
    maxMessageIndex?: number;
    partFilter?: (part: { type: string }, msgRole: string) => boolean;
    filteredPartIds?: Set<string> | null;
    unmappedLabel?: string; // defaults to "other"
  },
): ComponentAggregation
```

This iterates messages up to `maxMessageIndex` (default: all), applies `partFilter` and `filteredPartIds` filtering, looks up each part in `componentMapping`, and accumulates into `componentTokens` + `totalTokens`. Unmapped parts go to `unmappedLabel`.

#### Function 4: `buildComponentTimeline`
Unified version of `buildComponentTimeline` (componentisation.ts:391-445) and `buildStaticComponentTimeline` (static-componentisation.ts:62-100). They do the same thing; the only difference is `buildStaticComponentTimeline` iterates `Object.entries(mapping)` while `buildComponentTimeline` iterates `partInfo`. Both produce identical results.

```ts
export function buildComponentTimeline(
  conversation: Conversation,
  componentMapping: Record<string, string>,
  options?: {
    unmappedLabel?: string; // "other" by default
  },
): ComponentTimelineSnapshot[]
```

The old `conversationId` logging parameter is removed from this pure function. Callers who need logging can wrap it.

#### Function 5: `buildCumulativeChartData`
Replaces the per-message cumulative aggregation in StackedBarChartView.tsx (lines 65-98). Currently that code recomputes from scratch for each message index (O(n^2)). This function does it efficiently in a single pass.

```ts
export function buildCumulativeChartData(
  conversation: Conversation,
  componentMapping: Record<string, string>,
  components: string[],
  options?: {
    partFilter?: (part: { type: string }, msgRole: string) => boolean;
  },
): Array<Record<string, number> & { messageIndex: number; totalTokens: number }>
```

Returns one entry per message with cumulative token counts per component. This replaces the O(n^2) pattern with O(n).

#### Function 6: `computeTupleTokens`
Moved directly from componentisation.ts (lines 350-385). Signature stays the same.

```ts
export function computeTupleTokens(
  conversation: Conversation,
  dimensions: Record<string, DimensionData>,
  activeDimNames?: string[],
  options?: {
    maxMessageIndex?: number;
    filteredPartIds?: Set<string> | null;
    partFilter?: (part: { type: string }, msgRole: string) => boolean;
  },
): { tupleTokens: Record<string, number>; total: number }
```

#### Function 7: `computePercentages`
Replaces the inline percentage computation in WaffleChart.tsx, ComponentComparisonView.tsx, ai-summary.ts.

```ts
export function computePercentages(
  componentTokens: Record<string, number>,
  totalTokens?: number, // if omitted, computed as sum of values
): ComponentPercentage[]
```

Returns unsorted. Callers sort as needed (by tokens, by name, by category).

#### Function 8: `generateComponentCSV`
Moved from ai-summary.ts (lines 160-186). Unchanged signature.

```ts
export function generateComponentCSV(
  componentTimeline: ComponentTimelineSnapshot[],
  components: string[],
  conversation: Conversation,
): string
```

### Migration Plan

The migration is done in 5 sequential steps. Each step should be a separate commit that keeps the build green.

**Step 1: Create `src/aggregation.ts` with all functions and types.**
- Define `ComponentTimelineSnapshot`, `ComponentAggregation`, `ComponentPercentage` here.
- Implement all 8 functions listed above.
- Export `TUPLE_SEPARATOR`.

**Step 2: Update `src/componentisation.ts` to re-export from aggregation.**
- Remove `ComponentTimelineSnapshot` interface definition; re-export from aggregation.
- Remove `TUPLE_SEPARATOR` constant; re-export from aggregation.
- Remove `computeTupleTokens` function; re-export from aggregation.
- Remove `buildComponentTimeline` function body; replace with a wrapper that calls `aggregation.buildComponentTimeline` and adds the logging. The `componentiseConversation` function still calls it, so keep the logging wrapper private.
- This preserves all existing import paths (`from "@/componentisation"`), so no downstream changes are needed yet.

**Step 3: Update `src/static-componentisation.ts`.**
- Remove `buildStaticComponentTimeline` body; replace with `import { buildComponentTimeline } from "./aggregation"` and delegate. The static version has no `unmappedLabel` behavior (it uses the mapping directly, no "other" fallback), so pass `unmappedLabel: undefined` or just rely on the mapping being complete.
- Alternatively, since `buildStaticComponentTimeline` already has full mapping coverage (every part is mapped to `role.type`), we can just alias it: `export const buildStaticComponentTimeline = buildComponentTimeline;` with the same signature.

**Step 4: Update `src/ai-summary.ts`.**
- Remove `generateComponentCSV`; import from `"./aggregation"`.
- Change `import { computeTupleTokens, ... } from "./componentisation"` to import from `"./aggregation"` (or keep the re-export from componentisation).

**Step 5: Update React component call sites to use shared functions.**
This is the largest step but each sub-change is mechanical:

- **`src/components/MessageView.tsx`**: Replace inline `getTotalTokens()` with `getMessageTokenCount(message)` from aggregation.
- **`src/components/ConversationView.tsx`**: Replace `getMessageTokens()` with `getMessageTokenCount`. Replace the large `filteredSourceConversationComponents` loop body's token aggregation with `aggregateComponentTokens` (the turn-counting and timestamp logic stays in place since it is view-specific).
- **`src/components/ComponentsView.tsx`**: Replace the inline aggregation loop (lines 197-222) with `aggregateComponentTokens(conversation, effectiveMapping, { maxMessageIndex: currentMessageIndex, partFilter, filteredPartIds })`.
- **`src/components/StaticComponentsView.tsx`**: Replace inline loop (lines 56-74) with `aggregateComponentTokens(conversation, staticMapping, { maxMessageIndex: currentMessageIndex, partFilter })`.
- **`src/components/StackedBarChartView.tsx`**: Replace the O(n^2) `chartData` computation (lines 65-98) with `buildCumulativeChartData`.
- **`src/components/WaffleChart.tsx`**: Replace inline percentage computation with `computePercentages(componentTokens, totalTokens)`.
- **`src/components/ComponentComparisonView.tsx`**: Replace inline percentage computations with `computePercentages`.
- **`src/lib/export-builder.ts`**: Replace `buildAnalytics` token aggregation loop with `aggregateComponentTokens`.
- **`src/App.tsx`**: Replace the `sourceConversationComponents` mapping's token aggregation (lines 1388-1433) with `aggregateComponentTokens`. The timestamp/turn/messageComponent logic around it remains in App.tsx since it is specific to building `ConversationComponentData`.

### Key Design Decisions

1. **`partFilter` as a callback, not an enum.** The filtering logic varies between callers (some check `"all"` in a Set, some check static component IDs). A callback `(part, msgRole) => boolean` is the simplest common interface without coupling aggregation to filter UI concepts.

2. **`unmappedLabel` defaults to `"other"`.** Most callers bucket unmapped parts as "other". The export-builder and some views do this implicitly. Making it a default parameter covers most cases.

3. **`buildComponentTimeline` drops the logging parameter.** The function is pure. `componentisation.ts` wraps it with logging for the AI workflow. This keeps the aggregation module free of side effects.

4. **Re-export from `componentisation.ts` for backward compatibility.** Rather than updating every `import { ComponentTimelineSnapshot } from "@/componentisation"` in step 2, we re-export. This can be cleaned up later as a separate PR if desired.

5. **No new dependencies.** The module only imports from `./schema` (for `Conversation`, `Message` types) and uses the `DimensionData` type from componentisation (imported as a type-only import, or we move `DimensionData` to aggregation too -- but since `DimensionData` includes `componentTimeline: ComponentTimelineSnapshot[]` which references our type, it creates a cycle. Better to keep `DimensionData` in componentisation.ts and import it as a type in aggregation.ts).

Actually, looking at the `DimensionData` dependency more carefully: `computeTupleTokens` takes `Record<string, DimensionData>`. To avoid a circular import (aggregation imports DimensionData from componentisation, componentisation re-exports from aggregation), we should either:
- Move `DimensionData` to aggregation.ts as well (it is just a type), or
- Have `computeTupleTokens` accept a narrower type: `Record<string, { componentMapping: Record<string, string> }>` which is all it actually uses.

The second option is cleaner. `computeTupleTokens` only reads `dimensions[dimName]?.componentMapping[part.id]`. So its parameter type should be:

```ts
dimensions: Record<string, { componentMapping: Record<string, string> }>
```

This avoids any import from componentisation.ts, keeping aggregation.ts a leaf module that only depends on `schema.ts`.

### Risks and Mitigations

- **ConversationView.tsx filteredSourceConversationComponents** is the most complex call site because it mixes token aggregation with turn counting, timestamp tracking, and multi-dimension component filtering. The plan is to use `aggregateComponentTokens` only for the inner token loop, keeping the surrounding logic in place. If the call becomes awkward, it may be better to leave this one as-is initially and refactor in a follow-up.

- **StackedBarChartView O(n^2) to O(n)** changes the computation approach. Verify that the output matches exactly by comparing the chart data for a test conversation before and after.

### Critical Files for Implementation
- `/Users/srihari/work/nilenso/context-viewer/src/aggregation.ts` - New module to create with all pure aggregation functions
- `/Users/srihari/work/nilenso/context-viewer/src/componentisation.ts` - Remove `buildComponentTimeline`, `computeTupleTokens`, `TUPLE_SEPARATOR`, `ComponentTimelineSnapshot`; replace with re-exports from aggregation
- `/Users/srihari/work/nilenso/context-viewer/src/static-componentisation.ts` - Replace `buildStaticComponentTimeline` with delegation to aggregation's `buildComponentTimeline`
- `/Users/srihari/work/nilenso/context-viewer/src/ai-summary.ts` - Remove `generateComponentCSV`; import from aggregation
- `/Users/srihari/work/nilenso/context-viewer/src/components/ComponentsView.tsx` - Primary React consumer to migrate; pattern reference for updating other component call sites
